explanations.answer: The good news about the Lord Jesus
explanations.explanation: Acts 11:20 says it plainly: they were proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus. These men travel to a new city, and Jesus is the whole message. When the message is that good, you don't need a second topic.

explanations.answer: The laws God gave through Moses
explanations.explanation: "The law was given through Moses" (John 1:17), but that's not what verse 20 says these men bring. The text says they were proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus. That's the message they carried into Antioch. Keep your eyes on that phrase.

explanations.answer: The words of the prophet Isaiah
explanations.explanation: Isaiah saw a vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem (Isaiah 1:1), and his words matter. But Acts 11:20 doesn't say these men were bringing them to Antioch. What it says is that they were proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus. That's the message on the table here.

explanations.answer: Remain in the Lord with all their hearts
explanations.explanation: The BSB says Barnabas encouraged them all to "…abide in the Lord with all their hearts." That's the same idea as remain. He doesn't ask for half a heart or a heart on weekends. All their hearts, in one big batch.

explanations.answer: Return with him to Jerusalem at once
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say anything about going back to Jerusalem. Verse 22 says Jerusalem sent Barnabas to Antioch, and verse 23 says that when he arrived, he encouraged them all to "…abide in the Lord with all their hearts." So the encouragement is about staying with the Lord, not packing bags.

explanations.answer: Wait in Antioch for the apostles' word
explanations.explanation: Waiting for the apostles' word isn't in this verse. Acts 11:23 says Barnabas saw the grace of God, rejoiced, and encouraged them all to "…abide in the Lord with all their hearts." Nobody gets told to sit and wait for a message. The encouragement is to hold on to the Lord.
